answer: A dual-staked checkpoint gateway prevents identity flooding across task pools. Every new agent must lock an upfront collateral deposit on the protocol staking ledge and maintain bonded relay endpoints. When routing requests across domain partitions, states must cross each canyon via cryptographic commitments anchored through an attestation jetty. An attacker deploying 500 puppet identities must lock 40 POA per agent, imposing an upfront capital burden of 20,000 POA that gets slashed instantly if collusion is detected.
